properties.description: Tungsten oxide-based material, delaminated for 4 hours

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis of CWO
nodes.procedure: CWO was synthesized using a hydrothermal reaction (details in supplementary text, section 1, and fig. S3). The sharp peaks in x-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns from different batches indicate a highly crystalline structure matching a monoclinic CoWO4 phase.
nodes.source_text: We thus synthesized CWO using a hydrothermal reaction (supplementary text, section 1, and fig. S3). The sharp peaks in x-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns from different batches indicate a highly crystalline structure matching a monoclinic CoWO4 phase

nodes.name: Anion Exchange Delamination of CWO
nodes.procedure: The resulting CWO material was dispersed in an 0.1 M potassium hydroxide (KOH) aqueous solution for 48 hours to perform the WO₄²⁻ → OH⁻ and H₂O anion exchange. This study revealed the critical role of K⁺ to balance the delamination and the need for H₂O and hydroxide to enable the anion exchange.

unit_operations.name: KOH Dispersion
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: dispersing the resulting CWO material in an 0.1 M potassium hydroxide (KOH) aqueous solution for different time periods (48 hours optimal)

nodes.source_text: dispersing the resulting CWO material in an 0.1 M potassium hydroxide (KOH) aqueous solution for different time periods... optimal Co/W ratio and OH⁻ and H₂O trapping... achieved for 48-hour delaminated samples

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in 0.5 M H2SO4 H-cell
nodes.source_text: Linear-sweep voltammetry of Co-based catalysts at 5 mV s−1 in 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte... A minimum 288-mV overpotential at 10-mAcm−2 current density was obtained for CWO-del-48 [no iR correction]... The Faradaic efficiency for O2 generation was 96.6±5.2% at 10-mAcm−2 current density... Tafel analysis reveals a slope of 85 mV decade-1 for CWO-del-48

nodes.description: PEMWE performance and stability at 80°C, 1 A/cm2
nodes.source_text: The polarization curve of CWO-del-48-based cells reaches a nominal current density of 1.8 Acm−2 at 2 V... During electrolysis at a fixed current density of 0.2 Acm−2, the voltage range (1.53 to 1.56 V)... retained for at least >278 hours... stable performance with a stabilized cell voltage of ∼1.77 V during 608 hours... ICP-OES analysis of the anolyte reveals a Co concentration of ∼1.7 ppm after 20 hours

nodes.source_text: Tafel analysis reveals a slope of 85 mV decade-1 for CWO-del-48 versus 63 mV decade-1 for IrO2 and 227 mV decade-1 for CWO.

nodes.description: Chronopotentiometry stability test in H-cell at 10 mA/cm2
nodes.source_text: CWO-del-48 exhibits the highest stability (>175 hours) over commercial Co3O4 and CWO (Fig. 4C) in a H-cell at 10 mA cm−2... The resulting stability number (S number) after 100 hours of stability test at 10 mA cm−2 is 14771±768... ∼2.76 parts per million (ppm) concentration of dissolved Co ions in anolyte after 100 hours of chronopotentiometry

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD patterns of CWO show sharp peaks matching monoclinic CoWO4 phase; CWO-del shows regular shift in 111 peak indicating defects while retaining bulk monoclinic phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The sharp peaks in x-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns from different batches indicate a highly crystalline structure matching a monoclinic CoWO4 phase ... Powder XRD patterns show a regular shift in the most intense 111 peak (table S7), indicating the generation of defects or strain in the crystal structure

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and STEM images show cube-like shape for CWO transitioning to delaminated flake-like shape for CWO-del with comparable particle size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) images show a shape transition from a cube-like CWO ... to a delaminated, flake-like shape after KOH treatment (figs. S22 and S23)

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals missing regular (010) crystal plane in CWO-del-48 indicative of defects from WO4^2- leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images reveal the missing regular (010) crystal plane in CWO-del-48 (figs. S22 and S25), indicative of defects arising from WO4^2- leaching

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ Raman shows bathochromic shift (5-10 cm^-1) for Co-O (~690 cm^-1) and W-O (~886 cm^-1) peaks with increasing delamination time; intensity ratio Co-O/W-O increases up to 48 hours.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex situ Raman spectroscopy measurements ... reveal a bathochromic shift (~5 to 10 cm^-1) for both Co-O (~690 cm^-1) and W-O (~886 cm^-1) peaks with increasing delamination time (Fig. 2A)

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA-MS shows ~16 wt% weight loss for CWO-del-48 over 166-396°C due to water and/or OH- ions, with four distinct peaks indicating different water coordination environments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with mass spectroscopy (TGA-MS) revealed an ~16% weight loss for CWO-del-48 over a 166° to 396°C range due to water and/or OH- ions

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS of CWO deconvolutes into metal oxygen (OM) at 528.55 eV and lattice oxygen (OL) at 530.33 eV. CWO-del-48 shows four peaks: OM, OL, hydroxide (OOH) at 531.6 eV, and water (OH2O) at 533.1 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O 1s peak of nondelaminated samples deconvolutes into two peaks at 528.55 and 530.33 eV, which correspond to metal oxygen (OM) and lattice oxygen (OL). CWO-del-48 spectra, on the other hand, require deconvolution into two additional peaks corresponding to hydroxide (OOH), at 531.6 eV and water species (OH2O, at 533.1 eV)

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms increasing W leaching over delamination time with negligible change in Co concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) measurements confirm increasing W leaching over time but negligible change in Co concentration

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM EDX mapping shows uniform distribution of Co and W throughout pristine and delaminated nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-annular angle dark-field STEM (HAADF-STEM) images, and respective energy-dispersive xray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping of Co and W, show the uniform distribution of Co and W throughout the pristine and delaminated nanocrystals

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS spectra indicate reduction in Co/W atomic ratio after delamination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) spectra indicate a reduction in the Co/W atomic ratio after delamination

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM reveals missing planes and corresponding defects in CWO-del-48.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, atomic force microscopy (AFM) reveals missing planes and corresponding defects in CWO-del-48

nodes.characterization_summary: iDPC-STEM shows regular atomic arrangement in CWO but substantial vacancies in CWO-del-48 due to WO4^2- leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CWO samples exhibit a regular atomic arrangement of Co, W, and O atoms ... CWO-del-48, on the other hand, reveals a substantial number of vacancies due to WO4^2- leaching

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR reveals HO-H stretching and H-O-H bending vibrational modes with increasing intensity upon delamination, indicating higher density of trapped and bridged water and hydroxide groups.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) measurements. These reveal HO-H stretching and H-O-H bending vibrational modes with increasing intensity upon delamination

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows ~2.76 ppm dissolved Co ions in anolyte after 100 hours chronopotentiometry at 10 mA cm^-2, with 0.3 ppm leaching during OCP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS) reveals that Co leaching remains unchanged after 50 hours of OER ... with an ~2.76 parts per million (ppm) concentration of dissolved Co ions in anolyte after 100 hours
